Shift each subject's dates by a random offset

Source: R/anon_subject.R
anon_subject_dates.Rd

Gives every subject one random offset, in whole days, and shifts all of that subject's dates in every dataset by it. Intervals within a subject (time since dose, study days, visit windows) are unchanged, while calendar dates no longer line up between subjects or with real dates. This is the "date offsetting" technique described in EMA's Anonymisation Report Form Instructions: a random offset, with the same offset applied to all dates for each participant.

Usage

anon_subject_dates(
  data,
  key = "USUBJID",
  vars = NULL,
  max_days = 365,
  min_days = 30,
  partial = c("shift", "remove"),
  keep_secrets = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, a named list of data frames linked by key, or the result of an earlier step such as anon_subject_dates(). Datasets without the key column are returned unchanged.

key

Name of the subject identifier column.

vars

Names of date columns to shift. By default, every character or factor column whose name ends in DTC (any case; ISO 8601 dates, as in SDTM) and every Date or POSIXct column, in each dataset that has the key. In SDTM supplemental qualifier datasets (with QNAM and QVAL), QVAL values that are ISO 8601 dates with more than a bare year are shifted too (year-only values are left alone because they can't be told apart from numbers; a warning names the columns where they were kept). In columns not named *DTC, such as QVAL or a result column given in vars, only the values that are dates are shifted and other values are kept; bare four-digit numbers are kept too (with a warning), unless every value of the column, in every dataset, is a bare year (such as a column of birth years). Columns given in vars must be Date, POSIXct, or character or factor columns of ISO 8601 dates.

max_days, min_days

Each subject's offset is drawn uniformly from the whole numbers between min_days and max_days days, earlier or later. Defaults 30 and 365; max_days can be at most 3650. A warning is given when the range is so narrow, or includes 0, that offsets are easy to guess or some subjects keep their real dates.

partial

How to handle partial ISO 8601 dates in character columns: "shift" (default) or "remove" (replace them with the column's missing value). With "shift", a year-and-month date ("2014-03", or SDTM "2014-03--T08:00" with the time kept) moves the middle of the month by the subject's offset and keeps month precision; a year-only date ("2014", or SDTM "2014---15" with the day kept) moves by whole years, at least one, in the direction of the offset, so the real year is never kept. Both ends of an interval ("2014-01-02/2014-01-05") are shifted.

keep_secrets

Logical. If TRUE, keep each subject's offset; read it with anon_secrets(). Default FALSE.

seed

Optional seed for the random assignment, for reproducible tests. Anyone with the seed and the original data can rebuild the mapping, so do not set it for data you share. The global random number state is restored afterwards.

Value

An object of class "anon_deid_step", as for anon_subject_ids().

Details

Full ISO 8601 dates move by exactly the subject's offset and keep their format and any time part. Date columns keep their type, and POSIXct columns keep their type, time zone and clock time (the calendar date moves, so a shift across a daylight saving change keeps 08:00 at 08:00). Column attributes such as variable labels are kept; value labels (haven labels) are dropped, and haven user-defined missing values (na_values, na_range) in the key and date columns become plain missing values. A clock time that doesn't exist on the new date (inside a daylight saving gap) moves forward by the gap. Study day variables (--DY) are not changed and stay consistent with the shifted full dates, because each subject's dates all move together.

Year-and-month dates are shifted from the middle of the month, and year-only dates by whole years, so the order between a partial date and a full date of the same subject can change (for example a start month can end up after an end date).

Dates in rows without a key cannot be tied to a subject's offset and are removed, with a warning. In *DTC columns, values that are not recognised ISO 8601 dates, or whose year would fall outside 0001-9999, are removed with a warning; this includes a month and day without a year ("--12-15"). Time-only values ("-----T07:15") and durations ("P1D") have no date and are kept. Text columns given in vars must contain at least one recognised date. Datasets without the key column (for example trial-level domains such as TS, TV and TA) are left unchanged and listed in the log; their real trial dates can narrow down subjects' offsets. A warning lists any other column in a keyed dataset that holds dates but was not shifted: Date or POSIXct columns left out of vars, numeric columns with a SAS date format (in a separate warning; convert them to Date or POSIXct to shift them), and text columns with ISO 8601 dates as whole values, or dates inside text (which can't be shifted) written as ISO 8601, with a month name (05JAN2014, UNK-JAN-2014, 5 Jan 2014, Jan 5, 2014, JAN2014) or as numbers with separators (01/05/2014, 1/5/14, 01.05.2014, 2014/01/05), including the values kept in mixed columns such as QVAL. Other formats, such as 20140105, are not detected. It also lists any dataset without key that has such columns or a column named like key in another case.

Random numbers come from R's random number generator; see anon_subject_ids(). Run this before or after anon_subject_ids(); each subject keeps one offset either way. Under HIPAA, HHS does not address date shifting directly, but Safe Harbor removes all elements of dates except the year, so shifted dates do not meet it; see the package README.

Examples

data <- list(
  dm = data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "b"), RFSTDTC = c("2014-01-02", "2013-07-19")),
  pc = data.frame(USUBJID = c("a", "a", "b"),
                  PCDTC = c("2014-01-02T08:00", "2014-01-03T09:30", "2013-07-19T08:00"))
)
anon_subject_dates(data)$data
#> $dm
#>   USUBJID    RFSTDTC
#> 1       a 2013-08-02
#> 2       b 2013-10-19
#> 
#> $pc
#>   USUBJID            PCDTC
#> 1       a 2013-08-02T08:00
#> 2       a 2013-08-03T09:30
#> 3       b 2013-10-19T08:00
#>
